title: PharmTech AI Pulse Check: Why Pharma Should Weigh In on FDA's Generative AI Paper
source_used: PharmTech (lead only, 852 characters); background on the FDA paper from Cooley LLP (28 Sep 2026)
key_facts: The FDA's discussion paper on generative AI for medical devices has a public comment period through 19 Oct 2026.
PharmTech's AI Pulse Check panelists argue the industry's response matters beyond device regulation, and that pharma manufacturing, quality and regulatory professionals have a stake.
Gourav Pandey, R&D quality lead at Takeda, predicts comments will cluster around three themes, first definition and scope, because generative AI behaves non-deterministically.

Background (Cooley): FDA's device centre CDRH released the paper on 18 Aug 2026; it is not guidance; it proposes a two-axis risk framework and a 'competency-based' premarket evaluation modelled on how clinicians are assessed.
quote_evidence: The deadline to comment on FDA's generative AI paper is Oct 19, 2026.
Gourav Pandey, R&D quality lead at Takeda, predicts comments will cluster around three themes.
why_it_matters_hint: The FDA is still asking for input on how to regulate generative AI in medical devices, and the deadline is days away.
event_date: FDA paper released 18 Aug 2026; comments close 19 Oct 2026; PharmTech piece 16 Oct 2026.
notes: PharmTech text cut off after the first theme; only the lead was read. Panelists Richard Jaenisch and Florin Muraru are not named in the entry because their positions are not given in the readable text.
